name: United Arab Emirates

income_tax.summary: No federal or emirate-level personal income tax on employment or self-employment income (PwC, reviewed 9 Sep 2026). Non-GCC expatriates pay no UAE social security; only a flat unemployment-insurance fee (AED 5 or 10 a month) applies. A person running a business pays 9% UAE Corporate Tax only if business turnover exceeds AED 1 million.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: No self-employment social security for non-GCC nationals. Self-employment through a licensed business can come under 9% Corporate Tax above AED 1,000,000 turnover; wages and personal investment income do not count toward that turnover.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Dubai has no income-based local tax. Unemployment insurance: AED 5 per month (basic salary up to AED 16,000) or AED 10 per month (above), from 1 Jan 2023.

regimes.name: Dubai Virtual Working Programme (remote work visa)
regimes.description: One-year Dubai residence visa for remote workers employed by or owning a company outside the UAE. Holders live in the UAE with 0% personal income tax because the UAE levies none. Officially reported minimum is USD 5,000 a month; older and third-party sources still quote USD 3,500. Covers local work: the UAE levies no personal income tax at all, so pay for work done while living in the UAE is untaxed (PwC).
regimes.duration_note: Valid for one year, renewable on re-application; no cap on renewals found.

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: no visa-free right to work. A remote worker employed by a non-UAE company, or owning one, can apply for the Dubai Virtual Working Programme (one-year residence visa, reported minimum USD 5,000 a month). A skilled employee normally enters on a UAE work permit and residence visa sponsored by a local employer; the Golden Visa is a longer-term route (see data/jurisdictions/ARE.json). Citizenship does not change the route.
open_questions: Employee residence routes (work permit, Golden Visa) are described only in the existing jurisdiction file, not re-verified here.
